medicaid_adult_income_limit_note: FSSA: "HIP (Indiana's Medicaid for adults with income up to 138% of the Federal Poverty Level)"; FSSA HIP page (2026 limits): "Individuals with annual incomes up to $22,026.00 may qualify"; "The plan covers Hoosiers ages 19 to 64 who meet specific income levels."
enhanced_ptc_status_note: Per KFF (page dated Aug 3, 2026), the enhanced premium tax credits expired at the end of 2025; KFF cites that expiration as a factor in proposed 2027 rate increases and mentions no extension or restoration for 2027. No extension found in KFF material as of Oct 2026.
notes_unverified: OE dates: CMS/CCIIO statement dated July 27, 2026 says "Open Enrollment at the Federally-facilitated Marketplace will begin on November 1, 2026 and end on January 15, 2027" and that HHS "has not altered the dates for the Open Enrollment period contained in 45 CFR 155.410(e)(4)"; the HealthCare.gov dates-and-deadlines page (curl-fetched this run) also lists Nov 1 start, Dec 15 for Jan 1 coverage, Jan 15 end. BUT CMS's fact sheet for the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule says the Federal platform OEP would be Nov 1 - Dec 15 starting PY2027. Conflict is unresolved beyond the July 2026 statement (court orders in City of Columbus v. Kennedy struck/stayed some provisions; whether the OE provision was among them was not directly verified). Recommend rechecking healthcare.gov before publishing.

Exchange type: Indiana is treated as federally-facilitated (HealthCare.gov) based on in.gov state pages (Indiana healthcare reform site / SPD page listing the Federally Facilitated Marketplace) seen via search results; the healthcare.gov/indiana page itself did not state this. Not directly confirmed by a CMS exchange-type table in this run.

medicaid_expanded=true is inferred from FSSA wording that HIP is Indiana's Medicaid for adults up to 138% FPL (ACA adult-expansion threshold); the fetched FSSA text did not use the word 'expansion'. KFF expansion tracker (Oct 1, 2026) was image-based and unreadable; medicaid.gov Indiana page returned 404.
FSSA FPL chart (based on 2026 FPL) footnotes HIP Plus as "133 percent + 5 percent income disregard"; FSSA's older policy manual cites 133%. Monthly limit for 1 person on chart: $1,835.50.

Verified context (not a schema field): FSSA HIP work requirements page: "Beginning January 1, 2027, Indiana Medicaid will begin enforcing work requirements" for HIP members ages 19-64, not pregnant, not enrolled in/eligible for Medicare; applies to new applicants and redeterminations initiated on or after Jan 1, 2027; 80 hours/month qualifying activity or income of $580/month (7.25 x 80).
State subsidy/reinsurance: no Indiana 1332 reinsurance waiver or state-funded premium subsidy was found in sources checked; left null rather than asserting a negative.
Verified context (not a schema field): KFF (Aug 3, 2026) reports proposed 2027 marketplace premium increases (median ~15% across 276 insurers per KFF search summary, not confirmed on fetched page).
